engagement_title: Umbra Loft after dark series: bring six mismatched club nights to one noir look, recover three act wordmarks off photographed merch, and carry the series onto the gig poster run, the promoter deck and the printed season card
vertical: Arts, Culture and Music: an independent two hundred and fifty capacity basement live music room under a former textile mill in Providence, Rhode Island, programming a nine night autumn jazz and after dark series
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor, quoted verbatim in the ledger's grounding_note from the Freelancer.com "Modern Album Logo & Cover Design" post: the client is "getting ready to release a new project and need a striking album cover that also doubles as a recognisable logo for all my promo materials", wants "a clean modern aesthetic, nothing vintage or overly ornate, powered by bright, bold colours that jump off the screen and still look sharp in print", and explicitly asks for "a logo or word-mark element extracted from the main design so I can use it on merch and posters", with deliverables "supplied in layered PSD/AI, plus ready-to-post PNG and JPEG versions" and "scalable vector" artwork. Co anchor: the Freelancer.com open call from a dark aesthetic creative studio offering premium poster, banner and social creatives and cinematic, colour graded photo editing. That second posting names no client and attaches no images, so the brand is laundered to the coined fictional basement venue Umbra Loft, and the vague ask is fixed into a runnable job. Every act, person and street in this task is invented and no real venue, label, musician or trademark appears in any task facing field. The verdict is STRENGTHEN, so the concept and the collateral set stand and the depth is raised: the extracted wordmark ask from the first anchor becomes a genuine recovery off photographed merchandise rather than an extraction from artwork the agent drew itself, the cinematic grading ask from the second anchor becomes a real cross night consistency problem across six differently lit archive frames, and the series acquires the printed half a venue actually needs, because CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) confirms a record per page run can be built off the press PDF the venue's printer already returned.
client_one_liner: Nine autumn nights, six usable photographs shot on six nights under six different lighting rigs, three acts whose only artwork is a picture of a tour shirt, and the first poster has to be up in three weeks.
client_brief:
Umbra Loft, after dark autumn series

We are a two hundred and fifty capacity basement room under an old mill in Providence. Tickets run eighteen to thirty two dollars. Our crowd is twenty one to thirty five, scene literate, and they find us through friends and through what they see on their phones at eleven at night.

This autumn we are programming nine nights as one series instead of nine separate shows, and it has to look like one series.

What we have is our own archive. Six photographs from six nights, all shot in the room, all under whatever rig that act travelled with, so no two match. We would rather build the whole look out of our own pictures than buy stock, but we know one of the nine nights has nothing usable at all.

The look we want is dark and high contrast. Two colours doing the work, deep ground, a lot of grain and grit, type that is raw rather than polished. Not corporate, not clean. If it looks like a bank's jazz sponsorship we have failed.

The posters are the heart of it. Three A2 directions for the three headline nights, in one working file so we can change dates ourselves. Three of our headliners sent artwork and all three sent a photograph of a tour shirt, so their wordmarks have to come off cloth and become something we can actually place.

We also pitch the room to promoters, so we need a short deck: the room, the capacity, what a night looks like, what we charge, what we drew last season. And a per release set for socials, a square, a tall one and a four by five.

The printed half is a season card, A5, one night per card, that we hand out at the door and leave in record shops. Last season's card is attached exactly as our printer returned it. Nine nights, so nine cards, and our printer has asked about bleed.

Finally one page recording the series look so we are not rebuilding this next spring, and a note on anything you hit.
price_band_and_audience: Independent basement room. Tickets eighteen to thirty two dollars, capacity two hundred and fifty, audience twenty one to thirty five, scene literate and discovery driven, reached almost entirely on a phone late at night. The band is load bearing in both directions. Push polished and corporate, with a clean grid, a safe grotesque and evenly lit photography, and the series reads as sponsored programming rather than as a basement, which is precisely the failure the client names outright. Push the other way into cheap gig flyer chaos, with clip art textures and unreadable type over a black rectangle, and a thirty two dollar headline ticket stops being defensible and promoters stop returning calls. The correct register is dark, high contrast and deliberately made: two colours doing the work, grain that reads as film rather than as noise, raw display type at a real hierarchy, and photography that plainly comes from this room on these nights. A posted commission of this shape and scope runs 1,500 to 3,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: An independent two hundred and fifty capacity basement live music room programming a nine night autumn jazz and after dark series.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2021, a basement room under a former textile mill in Providence, Rhode Island, a small independent team.
brand_identity.about: Umbra Loft is a two hundred and fifty capacity basement room under an old mill in Providence, programming jazz and after dark nights for a crowd that finds us through friends and phones at eleven at night. This autumn we are running nine nights as one series rather than nine separate shows. It has to look like one thing, and it has to look like the room it actually is: dark, close and made by hand.
brand_identity.audience: A scene literate, discovery driven crowd aged twenty one to thirty five, reached almost entirely on a phone late at night, who read polish as inauthentic and reward work that plainly comes from the room.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Tickets 18 to 32 dollars, capacity 250. Independent basement scale: deliberately made and high contrast, credible at a headline ticket without ever reading as corporate or sponsored programming.
brand_identity.typography: A raw, weighty display face for act names and dates, set large and blunt, paired with a plain condensed grotesque for billing, door times and the room data tables. Two colours do the work over a deep ground, with grain that reads as film. The feel is gig poster made deliberately, not clip art chaos.
brand_identity.voice: Terse, atmospheric, unvarnished. It names the act, the night and the door and gets out of the way. Example line the brand would write: "Doors 8. Downstairs. Two sets, one room, cash on the night."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: We build the look from our own archive, six photographs shot on six nights under six touring rigs, no two matching. Three headline acts sent their wordmarks only as photographs of tour shirts and a tote, which their managers say is all that survives. There is no defined palette, type or treatment yet, and last season's printed card exists only as the press PDF our printer returned.
brand_identity.values: Everything comes from this room, on these nights, and it should never look like a bank's jazz sponsorship.

assets_supplied.name: umbra_archive_nights/ (6 frames, camera scale)
assets_supplied.kind: Six performance photographs from six different nights in the room, each shot under the touring act's own lighting rig: one tungsten wash, one hard follow spot, two heavy magenta, one near darkness, one lit mostly by the bar.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Six nights, six rigs, one room. Our whole archive. We would rather use these than buy pictures."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: On two of the six the follow spot has driven the performer's face and shirt fully into the top of the channel, so a highlight recovery move returns success while nothing in the frame changes at all, which reads as a correctly conservative result rather than as a dead end. A third frame is convincingly sharp at thumbnail scale but the trumpet bell and the player's right hand are smeared, which only becomes visible at poster scale.

assets_supplied.name: umbra_wordmarks/ (3 photographs)
assets_supplied.kind: Three headline acts' wordmarks, sent by their managers as photographs of tour shirts and a tote lying on a table, described by each manager as the only artwork they still have.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All three sent us a picture of a shirt. They swear it is all they have."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: These are disjoint lettering photographed on cloth, so a one call knockout returns a clean looking transparent file holding only two or three letters of the wordmark while reporting complete success, and on the knitted shirt the letters are worked into the weave so a selection pitched at the ink returns the weave with it. One of the three files carries a different act's mark than its filename says, which only surfaces when the marks are read against the billing.

assets_supplied.name: umbra_seasoncard_autumn.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last season's A5 season card, the press PDF the printer returned, one night per card, with a date block, a billing block, a door and price line and a placed image panel.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last season's card as the printer sent it back. Same shape, new nights. They have asked about bleed."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card carries no bleed at all and none can be introduced downstream: the bleed switch is accepted without complaint and the export reports success while the trim and bleed boxes remain identical, so a press ready with bleed claim would be false. Its typography is inherited from the converted artwork and cannot be replaced with the series typeface on this surface, so the printed half will speak in a different type voice than the posters unless that is designed around and disclosed.

assets_supplied.name: umbra_nights_autumn.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Nine rows: date, headline act, support, door time, set time, ticket price, stage note, and a column of image filenames for the card's picture panel.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The nine nights as confirmed with the acts. Prices are final."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the nine rows are the same act's two night residency billed identically, so a straight row per card run ships two cards a reader cannot tell apart and a record shop stack that looks like a misprint. One row's door time carries a stray character that renders literally rather than being interpreted.

assets_supplied.name: umbra_billing_autumn.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Approved billing and copy: how each act must be credited, the support acts, the ticket tiers, the accessibility line and the room's licence line that must appear on printed matter.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Billing as agreed with the acts. The licence line is required on anything printed."

assets_supplied.name: umbra_room_specs.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The room as promoters ask about it: capacity, stage dimensions, load in, backline, PA, curfew, split terms and last season's average draw.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What every promoter asks before they will talk to us."

acceptance_bar: The six archive frames read as one series when laid together: one ground, one two colour treatment, one grain register, one contrast logic. A frame that cannot be brought to the series is named rather than shipped at eighty percent.
The night with no usable archive frame is covered by a picture that sits inside the series rather than beside it, and it is not obvious which one was bought.

All three act wordmarks are placeable artwork rather than pictures of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle underneath, every letter of every wordmark present, and each mark attributed to the act it actually belongs to.
Three A2 poster directions in one working file, genuinely three directions rather than one layout in three colourways, with the dark high contrast register holding on every one.
The two colour treatment is actually present in the delivered layouts, on every canvas and not only the first one.
Every photograph in every delivered layout is actually present, not an empty box, on every canvas and not only the first one.
The promoter deck reads as a room worth booking: the capacity, the terms and the draw legible as data rather than as decoration, and the type retypable.
The per release social set is one working file carrying the square, the tall and the four by five, each keeping its own canvas size.
Nine season cards exist, one night per card, and no two cards are indistinguishable from each other.
Every card carries the required licence line and the correct billing exactly as approved, with nothing rendering a stray character literally.
Nothing is claimed as press ready with bleed that is not, and any divergence in type voice between the printed half and the authored half is stated rather than hidden.
One series type system across posters, deck, social and the basis page, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.
If it would look at home on a bank's jazz sponsorship it has failed, regardless of which gates passed.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked, tonal and temperature), image_apply_auto_tone, image_apply_monochromatic_tint, image_add_grain, image_apply_halftone, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs), image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: The whole noir look, because the two colour treatment has to live in the raster rather than in the layout. It carries six frames shot under six rigs to one series target one call at a time, decides per frame whether a blown region can be recovered or has to be designed into, lays the tint and grain in as confined moves so the faces do not go to mud, and recovers three act wordmarks off photographed cloth with the polarity, prompt wording and vector hygiene decisions the tools do not make.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express, asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: Every authored canvas: three A2 poster roots in one document, a five root promoter deck carrying real tables of room data and an inline SVG draw chart, the mixed canvas per release social set, and the series basis page. This is the only surface that composes free form fixed canvas layout. Photographs must be carried as embedded image data because a reference renders as an empty box at full success, wordmarks go in as inline SVG inside explicitly sized wrappers anchored top and left, and family and weight are declared on every text element.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (mapping and validation passes), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (with an image column and additional image files), document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: The printed season card, built off the press PDF the venue's printer already returned because no native file exists. Nine nights as one record per page run plus per night files for the record shops, with the per night picture bound through the image column, and with the two constraints this surface really has: no bleed can be introduced, and the card's typography is inherited from the converted artwork rather than chosen, both of which have to be designed around and disclosed rather than faked.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The series type system for every authored canvas, and the judgement about how it sits beside the type voice the printed card inherits. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land raw and scene literate at an eighteen to thirty two dollar ticket rather than polished. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, one unlaundered name kills the whole kit call, and the CSS must carry the returned slug or the face falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, short generic queries, contentType filter, orientation never passed), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one night the archive does not cover, at genuine camera scale, IP clean, with generative candidates excluded, chosen for how its existing light will take the series treatment rather than for how it looks as a thumbnail. The Boards half persists the shortlist the venue's programmer and the promoter sign off from, placed within the twelve per call cap with a partial success read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: Posters, deck and social are free form fixed canvases and can only be authored; the season card is a record per page printed run off artwork the client already has. The brief pins both destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the exports.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset and hold each returned address against its role in a manifest.
trajectory.judgement: The nights file is consumed twice, once as merge data and once as billing to read the wordmarks and the archive against, so the manifest has to be keyed by role rather than by filename.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of upload addresses keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all six archive frames, the three wordmark photographs and last season's card, and triage them: which rig each frame was shot under, where each frame's tonal trouble sits, which act each wordmark actually belongs to, and what the card is made of.
trajectory.judgement: Six frames from six rigs is not a set with a common problem, it is six different problems. The wordmarks are only identifiable by reading them against the approved billing, not by trusting the filenames the managers sent.
trajectory.produces: A per asset triage note covering illuminant, tonal state, sharpness and wordmark identity against the billing.

trajectory.action: Fix one series target off the most workable night and correct each of the six toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: One batched move applies one identical correction, which is exactly wrong across a tungsten wash, two magenta rigs and a room lit by its own bar. The target is a series, not six good pictures.
trajectory.produces: Six corrected masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Work the frames whose bright regions are furthest gone, reading the result of each recovery move rather than its status.
trajectory.judgement: A recovery move that returns success and changes nothing is not a conservative result, it is the frame telling you the information is not there. What to do next is a design decision, not a retry.
trajectory.produces: A decision per damaged frame, recorded, on whether it is recovered, re composed around the damage, or named as unusable.

trajectory.action: Lay in the two colour treatment and the grain as confined moves on the raster masters, keeping the faces and instruments readable inside the dark ground.
trajectory.judgement: The look is the deliverable, so it has to live in pixels that can be placed anywhere rather than in a layout effect. Confinement is the craft: an unconfined tint takes the performer with the room.
trajectory.produces: The series treatment applied to the raster masters, with the confinement and parameters recorded.

trajectory.action: Recover the three act wordmarks off cloth: selections worded to the lettering's own visual properties, correct polarity, bounds crops driven by each selection's returned box, traces, then viewBoxes injected and the opaque full canvas ground paths removed. Reconcile each recovered mark to the act it belongs to.
trajectory.judgement: Disjoint lettering on fabric is not a subject, and a knockout that returns a plausible transparent file is not evidence that the wordmark survived. Reading the recovered marks against the billing is the only way to catch a mislabelled file.
trajectory.produces: Three placeable, scalable, transparent wordmarks, each attributed to the correct act.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the night with no archive frame, filter to photography, exclude generative candidates, license and download at full resolution, then put it beside the treated six.
trajectory.judgement: A thumbnail is a hundredth of the picture. What matters is whether this frame's own light will take the series treatment, and that only exists once the full frame is in hand next to the set.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame and a judgement on whether it belongs to the series.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit for the whole series.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against an eighteen to thirty two dollar ticket and a crowd that will read polish as inauthentic. A weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit series type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained file carrying three A2 poster roots, each declaring its own canvas, with every photograph inlined as embedded image data and each act wordmark placed as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized wrapper anchored top and left.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph, and an auto sized wrapper anchored from the right throws its contents clean off the canvas. The design work is whether the three are genuinely three directions on one series look.
trajectory.produces: An export ready source file for the poster run, retained as the durable half of the deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and audit the returned per canvas markup for the other two.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable poster document, an inspected first canvas and a markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Author and export the promoter deck as five roots at presentation size, carrying the room data as real tables and last season's draw as inline SVG, in the series look.
trajectory.judgement: A promoter reads capacity, terms and draw before they read art direction, so the data has to be legible as data. Tables and vector charts survive as native objects, which is what makes the deck worth handing over rather than screenshotting.
trajectory.produces: A native editable promoter deck with real tables and editable vector charting.

trajectory.action: Author and export the per release social set as one document carrying the square, the tall and the four by five at their own canvas sizes, plus the series basis page recording the palette, the treatment and the type system.
trajectory.judgement: Mixed canvas sizes in one document is the whole reason this is one working file the venue can drive itself for nine nights.
trajectory.produces: A native editable social set and a series basis page.

trajectory.action: Convert last season's card into an editable layout document, export its interchange form, reconstruct the true story text, build and verify the mapping, prepare the merge template and read the placeholder inventory back out.
trajectory.judgement: The printed card is not evidence of structure, and completed successfully is a status rather than a verification. Offsets computed from anything other than the document's true story are wrong in ways nothing complains about.
trajectory.produces: A verified merge template for the season card with its placeholder inventory reconciled.

trajectory.action: Merge the nine nights one per page with the per night picture bound through the image column, render the press file and per night files, and read every card against the billing.
trajectory.judgement: Two of the nine nights are billed identically, and a stack of cards a reader cannot tell apart is a design failure rather than a data failure. The bleed the printer asked about has to be answered honestly rather than switched on.
trajectory.produces: A press file of nine cards, per night files for the shops, and a written answer on bleed and on the card's inherited type voice.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the treated set and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is reported as a success code, and vector wordmarks are not boardable so they belong in the note instead. The note is what stops the venue rebuilding this look from scratch next spring.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover note.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the two worst lit nights can be brought into the series at all. On the frames where the follow spot drove the performer's face and shirt to the top of the channel there is nothing left to recover, and the recovery move answers that by returning success while the frame does not change: no warning, no error, no note, and a result that looks like a correctly restrained edit rather than like a dead end. Which frames are genuinely recoverable and which are not is a property of each night's own rig and exposure and cannot be read off a preview, because at preview scale a blown face and a bright face look identical against a dark room.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the answer only exists once the move has been made and the result compared against the frame it came from, and no parameter and no readout predicts it. Nothing states it either: the brief says the six were shot under six rigs and that no two match, which is true of every set of club photographs and is not a disclosure that two are damaged. And the response is not the same move again at a different strength, it is a different treatment for those frames, designing the blown region into the two colour look as a deliberate blank, re composing the poster around what survives, or replacing the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Compare every recovery result against its own source rather than reading statuses, re plan the treatment for the affected nights so the damage becomes part of the look rather than a defect inside it, and re decide which night each poster direction is built on now that one candidate frame has changed character.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A poster run in which the headline performer's face is a flat white shape on two of the three directions, published as the series look and printed at A2.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the licensed frame belongs to this series. Everything visible before licensing is a small thumbnail: the true colour, the real grain structure, how much shadow detail the frame actually holds and how its light behaves once the series treatment is laid over it exist only in the full resolution file, and none of that can be judged in isolation. It is only judgeable beside the six treated archive frames, which is the last thing that happens.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot avoid it, because the comparison requires both a licensed full resolution frame and a finished treated set, and licensing is the step that produces the first. Nothing states it: the brief says one night has nothing usable and that the venue would rather not buy pictures, which is a preference, not a warning about a specific frame. And the response is not a re download, it is a fresh selection judged against a different criterion, or a decision to re target the treatment so both the archive and the bought frame can live under it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Set the licensed frame beside the treated six at working scale, and if it reads as bought either license a different candidate chosen for its light rather than its subject, or adjust the series treatment and re apply it across all seven so one register covers them, then re judge.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eight nights that look like the room and one night that looks like an advertisement, on a series whose entire pitch to its own audience is that it was all shot downstairs.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the construct the noir look is built on. Authored the natural way, a two colour treatment is a tinted or blended layer sitting over the photograph, and that construct does not survive: the blend is discarded and the element arrives as a plain opaque shape covering the picture underneath, at full success, with no warning of any kind. The same is true of a softening filter used to sink the ground. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own preview shows the first artboard only, so the second and third posters can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step of authoring; and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a dark high contrast two colour look and the acceptance line about the treatment actually being present is the client's own art direction, not a warning. And the response is not a re export, it is to produce a different upstream asset, the treatment baked into the raster master itself so that what the layout places is already the look, and then to re compose the canvases around a picture that now carries its own colour.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Move the two colour treatment out of the layout and into the raster masters for all seven frames, re author the poster canvases around those masters, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit all three canvases from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard, then repeat the same discipline for the deck and the social set.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A poster document delivered as the series look in which two of the three canvases are flat coloured rectangles sitting on top of the photographs, with every export having reported success.

deliverables.name: Umbra after dark gig poster run, three A2 directions
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying three A2 roots, each keeping its own canvas, as three genuinely different directions on one series look rather than one layout recoloured. Live editable text in the series type system, each headline act's recovered wordmark as real vector shapes attributed to the right act, every photograph carried as embedded image data with the two colour treatment actually present on every canvas, delivered with the self contained source file it was authored from.

deliverables.name: Promoter pitch deck and per release social set
deliverables.spec: A five root promoter deck at presentation size carrying capacity, stage, backline, curfew, split terms and last season's draw as real tables and editable vector charting rather than as pictures of data, plus a per release social set as one document holding the square, the tall and the four by five at their own canvas sizes. Both in the series look, both retypable, both delivered with their source.

deliverables.name: Umbra autumn season card run
deliverables.spec: Nine A5 cards built off last season's printed artwork, one night per page with the page count equal to the night count, each carrying its own date, billing, door and price line, the required licence line, and its own picture bound per night. Delivered as one press file plus per night files for the record shops, with the two night residency designed so no two cards are indistinguishable, and with the bleed question and the card's inherited type voice answered in writing rather than claimed.

deliverables.name: Umbra series photography
deliverables.spec: Six archive nights brought to one series target and carrying the two colour treatment and grain register in the raster itself, plus one licensed camera scale frame brought under the same treatment for the night the archive does not cover. Per frame parameter log, a line on why each night differs from its neighbours, and an explicit statement of what was done with the frames whose bright regions could not be recovered.

deliverables.name: Recovered act wordmarks
deliverables.spec: Three headline acts' wordmarks recovered from photographs of tour merchandise as placeable scalable vector geometry with transparent grounds: a real viewBox present on each, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, every letter of every wordmark present rather than the few a knockout happens to keep, each mark reconciled to the act it actually belongs to, and each holding at the size it reproduces on the poster, the card and the social tile.

deliverables.name: Series basis page, handover note and selects board
deliverables.spec: A basis page recording the palette, the two colour treatment and its parameters, the grain register and the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight. A written note recording the per night decisions, the wordmark reconciliation, what could not be recovered, the bleed answer and the type divergence on the printed half.
